# `Q-7-1` — Missing Newline at End of File

> An input file does not end with a newline; one is added
> automatically.

## What this means

POSIX text files end with a newline. Most editors enforce this,
some tools rely on it, and several parsers behave subtly
differently when it is missing. Quarto's input handling tolerates
the omission — it adds a newline to the in-memory buffer before
parsing — but emits a warning so the discrepancy is visible.

The render still succeeds, and the file on disk is not modified.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **An editor that does not enforce a trailing newline** (some
  Windows editors, older versions of Notepad).
- **A file generated by a script** that wrote content without
  the final `\n`.
- **A file truncated mid-line** — investigate this case
  separately, since a truncation might mean missing content.

## How to fix

Add a newline at the end of the file. Most editors offer a
setting to enforce this for new and edited files. A one-shot fix
from the shell is `printf '\n' >> file.qmd`.
